/home/noah/.cargo/bin/forjar apply --yes > ap.out 2>&1; echo "apply rc=$?"
printf 'TAMPERED\n' > /tmp/forjar-dogfood/verify/m1/proj/hello.txt   # REAL drift

Verified 2/2 runs, in a fresh directory, for both tools.
confirmed.expected: forjar_drift should return the drift the CLI returns ({"drifted":true} with the hello-file finding) and forjar_plan should return unchanged:2 / to_create:0, exactly as `forjar drift --json` and `forjar plan --json` do on the identical config. Both MCP tools take a `path` argument documented in `forjar mcp --schema` as "Path to forjar.yaml", so the project being addressed is unambiguous; resolving that project's state against an unrelated directory (the server's cwd, which for an MCP stdio server is chosen by the client, not the project) makes the two arguments describe different projects. CONTROL 2 proves the comparison logic is correct and only the path resolution is wrong. drift is the tripwire tool the project relies on for CI/cron (policy.tripwire, `drift --tripwire`); a silent clean is the exact silent-green failure mode the project's own rules call the worst outcome.
confirmed.root_cause: The MCP handler layer passes the tool's `state_dir` argument through with the CLI's default value (the literal relative string "state") and resolves it against process cwd, instead of resolving it relative to the parent directory of the `path` argument it was given. The CLI never hits this because its cwd IS the project dir by construction. Confirmed by CONTROL 2: supplying an absolute state_dir produces the correct answer through the same code.
confirmed.fix_sketch: In the MCP tool handlers for forjar_drift and forjar_plan (and anywhere else a config `path` and a `state_dir` are both accepted), when `state_dir` is not supplied, default it to `Path::new(path).parent().join("state")` rather than `PathBuf::from("state")`; when it IS supplied and is relative, resolve it against the same parent. Add a regression test that calls the tool with an absolute config path from a different cwd and asserts the result equals the CLI's.

Verified 2/2 runs in a fresh directory.
confirmed.expected: An error result (isError:true, or a JSON-RPC error) carrying the same message the CLI produces - `cannot read state dir state: No such file or directory` - because the CLI is the authority on the identical inputs and it treats an unreadable state dir as a hard failure (exit 1), not as "no drift". The tool's own schema documents the output field as "drifted: Whether any drift was detected"; returning false when zero resources were compared is a false negative, not a detection. This is also what makes the path-resolution defect silent rather than loud: fixing only the path resolution would leave this class of false clean intact for genuinely unreadable/corrupt state.
confirmed.root_cause: The forjar_drift MCP handler treats a failure to enumerate/read the lock files in the state dir as an empty state set rather than propagating the Err, so the drift comparison runs over zero recorded resources and trivially finds nothing. The CLI's drift path propagates the same io::Error and exits 1.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Make the MCP drift handler propagate the state-dir read error into an MCP error result (isError:true with the io error text), matching the CLI. If "no state yet" is meant to be a legal answer, it must be a distinct field (e.g. {"state_present":false}) and must not be encoded as drifted:false.

confirmed.expected: `forjar apply --help` documents `--notify <NOTIFY>` as "FJ-317: POST JSON results to webhook URL after apply" - after apply, unconditionally - and the payload it does send contains a `total_failed` field, which is unreachable if the POST only happens on success. confirmed.fix_sketch: Move the --notify dispatch out of the success arm into the same common post-apply notification block that --notify-webhook uses, before the error is returned (or into a scope-guard / `finally`-style block), passing the real summary so total_failed is populated. confirmed.expected: `forjar apply --help` documents `--approval-webhook <APPROVAL_WEBHOOK>` as "FJ-546: POST for approval before applying (GitOps gate)". confirmed.expected: forjar's own behaviour in case B establishes the contract: a failed webhook delivery is reported as `Warning: webhook POST to <url> failed`. A 5xx rejection is a failed delivery - the receiver did not accept the notification - and must produce the same warning. Root cause is visible on the wire: the POST is issued by curl (the receiver logs User-Agent: curl/7.81.0) without --fail/--fail-with-body, so curl exits 0 on 5xx and forjar's exit-status check sees success.
confirmed.root_cause: The notification transport shells out to `curl` and decides success/failure purely from curl's process exit status. Without `--fail`, curl exits 0 for any completed HTTP transaction including 4xx/5xx, so only transport-level failures (exit 7 connection refused, exit 6 DNS, exit 52 empty reply) are ever reported.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Add `--fail-with-body` (or `-w '%{http_code}'` plus an explicit status check) to every curl invocation in the notification path, and include the HTTP status in the warning text: `Warning: webhook POST to <url> failed (HTTP 500)`. Same change fixes all the notify-* channels that share this helper.

confirmed.expected: The process should exit shortly after stdin reaches EOF. The server itself proves it intends these strings to be inserted - it computes a different value from the label for every field item - and it correctly camelCases everywhere else in the same session (textDocumentSync, completionProvider, triggerCharacters, interFileDependencies), so this one field is out of line with the server's own wire format.
confirmed.root_cause: The completion item is a hand-rolled struct serialised with serde's default field naming instead of the lsp-types CompletionItem (or a struct carrying #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]). The surrounding capability structs are correct, so only this type is missing the rename.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Add #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] to the completion item struct (or switch to lsp_types::CompletionItem), and add a test that asserts the serialised JSON of one item contains the key "insertText".

confirmed.summary: Every diagnostic the language server publishes is anchored at line 0, even when the server's own message text carries the real line number, so the editor squiggle is always on the first line of the file (and for validation errors the range is zero-width, i.e. invisible).
confirmed.repro:
rm -rf /tmp/forjar-dogfood/verify/l3 && mkdir -p /tmp/forjar-dogfood/verify/l3 && cd /tmp/forjar-dogfood/verify/l3
cat > dep2.yaml <<'EOF'
version: "1.0"
name: range-test

machines:
  local:
    hostname: localhost
    addr: 127.0.0.1
    user: noah
    arch: x86_64

resources:
  r1:
    type: file
    machine: local
    path: /tmp/forjar-dogfood/verify/l3/r1.txt
    content: "one\n"

  r2:
    type: file
    machine: local
    path: /tmp/forjar-dogfood/verify/l3/r2.txt
    content: "two\n"
    depends_on: [ghost-resource]
EOF
# drive `forjar lsp` with the drive.py harness (initialize -> initialized -> didOpen dep2.yaml)
# and print the textDocument/publishDiagnostics notification
confirmed.observed:
DIAG: [{"range": {"start": {"line": 0, "character": 0}, "end": {"line": 0, "character": 0}}, "severity": 1, "source": "forjar-lsp", "message": "resource 'r2' depends on unknown resource 'ghost-resource'"}]

For a YAML syntax error the range is equally wrong even though the message names the line:
DIAG: [{"range": {"start": {"line": 0, "character": 0}, "end": {"line": 0, "character": 80}}, "severity": 1, "source": "forjar-lsp", "message": "YAML parse error: did not find expected key at line 6 column 4, while parsing a block mapping at line 4 column 3"}]

Verified 2/2 runs in a fresh directory; identical for all broken configs tested.
confirmed.expected: The offending text is on line 22 (`depends_on: [ghost-resource]`), and in the YAML-error case the server has already computed "line 6 column 4" and embedded it in the message string it is publishing - it simply does not use it to build the `range`. A zero-width range at 0:0 also renders as no visible squiggle in most editors. The server advertises hoverProvider and position-aware completion, so it does track document positions.
confirmed.root_cause: The diagnostic constructor hard-codes Range::default()-style start/end; the parser's location (already available - it is interpolated into the message text) is never mapped to a Position, and validation errors carry no location at all because the validator returns plain strings.
confirmed.fix_sketch: For parse errors, use the error's line/column (0-based conversion) for the range instead of embedding it in the message. For semantic validation errors, have the validator return the offending resource id/key and locate it in the document text (a simple line scan for the resource key is enough) so the range points at the resource block.

rejected.id: mcp-plan-status-false-pending (partial reject: the forjar_status / forjar_trace / forjar_anomaly half)
rejected.why: The forjar_plan half reproduced and is CONFIRMED - it is merged into mcp-state-dir-cwd-relative-ignores-config-path. The forjar_status / forjar_trace / forjar_anomaly half is NOT a defect: those three tools take no config `path` at all (verified against `forjar mcp --schema` / tools/list - their only inputs are `machine` and `state_dir`), so there is nothing to resolve a state dir from, and their schema explicitly documents `state_dir` as 'State directory (default: "state")' - the same cwd-relative default the CLI uses. Returning machines:[] / trace_count:0 when pointed at a directory with no state is the documented behaviour, not a contradiction. The finding's own framing ('forjar_status/forjar_trace/forjar_anomaly do not even accept a config path from which the state dir could be derived') concedes this. Calling it a false report would require the tool to have been told which project was meant, and it was not.

rejected.id: mcp-graph-format-ignored-mislabeled (partial reject: the 'ascii/svg should render' claim)
rejected.why: The mislabelling half reproduced and is CONFIRMED as mcp-graph-format-echoes-a-format-it-did-not-produce. The claim that forjar_graph should render ascii/svg because the CLI can is wrong: the MCP tool's own schema documents format as 'Output format: "mermaid" (default) or "dot"', so those renderers are deliberately out of scope for this surface. Only the false `format` echo and the non-rejection of unknown values survive.

Not a rejection of the defect - the unbounded blocking reproduced 2/2 and is CONFIRMED - but the candidate's own evidence block was internally inconsistent and should not be trusted as written: it reported 'exit=0 elapsed=120s' with a warning naming port 18813 while the repro used port 18815, and claimed the exit code was 0. My measurement: the run must be killed by an external `timeout`, giving exit 124, and forjar's own exit code is never observed because it never terminates. The confirmed entry carries my re-measured numbers.

coverage_notes: Every one of the 16 candidate findings was re-run by hand against /home/noah/.cargo/bin/forjar (confirmed `forjar 1.12.3`) in fresh scratch dirs under /tmp/forjar-dogfood/verify/, at least twice each, with exit codes captured as `cmd > out 2>&1; rc=$?` (never through a pipe). All 16 reproduced at the behavioural level; two are narrowed rather than accepted whole (see rejected). The 16 candidates map to 16 confirmed entries after restructuring: the drift finding is SPLIT into two defects with different fixes (state_dir resolved against the server cwd, and drift answering 'not drifted' when the state dir cannot be read - the latter reproduces with cwd == project dir, so it is independent), the plan/status finding is MERGED into the path-resolution one (its status/trace/anomaly half rejected), and the graph finding is narrowed to the false `format` echo. WHAT WAS EXERCISED: apply on localhost with file + task resources (success and deliberate-failure paths); the --notify / --notify-webhook / --notify-slack / --notify-slack-webhook / --notify-webhook-v2 / --notify-custom-webhook / --notify-webhook-headers / --notify-custom-headers / --approval-webhook flags against local python HTTP receivers that log method, path, headers and body (including 200, 500, connection-refused and never-answering receivers); the MCP stdio server driven with hand-written JSON-RPC (initialize, tools/list, tools/call for drift, plan, status, trace, anomaly, show, graph) from both the project dir and an unrelated cwd, with and without an explicit absolute state_dir; the LSP over stdio (initialize, didOpen, textDocument/diagnostic, textDocument/completion, publishDiagnostics) on valid and on four kinds of broken config; and CLI validate/plan/show/fmt/drift/status/trace/graph as the authority for cross-checking. WHAT WAS NOT EXERCISED (so absence of findings there means nothing): any real host or any SSH transport - everything ran against 127.0.0.1 with a localhost machine; destroy / undo / migrate / rollback / state-rm / state-rekey / secrets / plugin (out of scope by the safety rules); the ~90 other --notify-* channels in `apply --help` beyond the seven listed above (given that two of the seven I did test are complete no-ops, the rest deserve a systematic sweep); the sibling approval flags --approval-required, --require-approval and --approval-timeout (only --approval-webhook was proven inert); the retry/custom-header behaviour --notify-webhook-v2 promises (unreachable - the flag sends nothing at all); parallel/wave execution, workspaces, recipes, imports and the v1.12 make/phony/import-makefile surface; and MCP tools forjar_validate and forjar_lint. I did not attempt to read forjar's source, so every root_cause is inferred from black-box behaviour plus the on-the-wire evidence quoted in each finding (e.g. the receiver-logged 'User-Agent: curl/7.81.0' for the notification transport, and the absolute-state_dir control for the MCP path resolution).
